personality_one_liner: A highly glanceable, high-contrast operational command center that prioritizes live metrics and minimizes driver distraction.

spacing.rule: Generous spacing but zero decorative padding. All touch targets MUST be at least 48x48pt for driving safety. Use strict grids for metrics.

dont's: No blur or glassmorphism. Automotive displays require maximum contrast, instant glanceability, and high rendering performance. Rely on solid surface hierarchy and borders.

screens.name: Cockpit Home
screens.purpose: A split-screen driving dashboard providing simultaneous access to map, media, and vehicle metrics.

states.empty: N/A - System always displays base metrics and map.
states.error: Error icon with 'Sensor Connection Lost' and a Retry button.

screens.layout: Landscape optimized. Left persistent rail (80px wide) for main navigation. Remaining screen is split: Left column (40% width) containing Vehicle Dashboard metrics at top and Media Now Playing card at bottom. Right column (60% width) is a full-bleed map view with a floating Voice Command mic overlaid on the top right.

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the Dark-First Utility guidelines. No blur or glassmorphism. Use solid surface hierarchy.
The app MUST be locked to horizontal/landscape layout, simulating a car dashboard.
Touch targets are critical for safety: Ensure all buttons, tabs, and interactive rows are at least 48x48pt.
Use 'Barlow Condensed' heavily for numbers, speed, RPM, ETA, and large metric displays to emulate physical car gauges.

The Home screen should not use standard bottom tabs. Instead, construct a persistent vertical rail on the left side, or use a Drawer navigator configured as a permanent side menu to mimic Rivian/CarPlay style layout.
Use high contrast colors: Obsidian background (#090A0C) with Amber/Orange (#FF6D00) for primary actions and active states.
Avoid decorative elements. Every visual component must serve a functional, glanceable purpose.
For the map screen, overlay a top-to-bottom gradient scrim if placing text directly over the map, or use solid floating panels for contrast.
